stories.headline: Fantasy football Week 10 inactives: Who's in and who's out?
stories.summary: Updated inactives and analysis based on the latest reports and official announcements leading up to kickoff.
stories.body:
Biggest injury concerns for Week 10
Players in Germany
Amon-Ra St. Brown, WR, Lions (ribs): The "Sun God" was limited at practice this week and is listed as questionable but appears likely to play in Week 10. He played through the injury last week and surpassed 16 fantasy points. St. Brown, who is a German citizen, will look to put on a show.

A.J. Brown, WR, Patriots (ankle/knee): Brown has been limited at practice this week and is questionable for Week 10. Brown averaged eight targets per game for the two times that he played on over 75% of snaps. Given all the missed time, he brings some risk. Still, if he suits up, fantasy managers should take the chance as he has a fantastic matchup against the Lions, who have allowed the fourth-most WR fantasy PPG.

Rhamondre Stevenson, RB, Patriots (knee): Stevenson was able to return in a limited fashion after missing practice to start the week. He is listed as questionable for Sunday. He has a tough matchup against the Lions, who have allowed the second-fewest fantasy PPG. They rank bottom six in rushing touchdowns and rushing yards per game allowed to RBs. He would be a risky flex option if he suits up. If he sits, Corey Kiner is the next man up. He would see volume, which is enough to have him in the flex range, but he should ideally be avoided if possible.

Hunter Henry, TE, Patriots (foot): Henry has been limited at practice this week but does not currently carry an injury designation for Week 10. That means he is expected to play. Henry is a TE1 worth starting against the Lions, who have allowed the most yards, touchdowns and fantasy points to tight ends.

Don't forget to check these out: Mike Clay's Playbook | Week 10 Buzz

Week 10 Rankings | Matchup rankings for Week 10

Official Sunday inactives should begin coming in approximately 90 minutes before the scheduled kickoff times: around 11:30 a.m. ET for the early games and 2:30 p.m. ET for the late-afternoon games.

Refresh often for the latest information.

Players with early starts
Harold Fannin Jr., TE, Browns (groin): While Fannin was limited at practice this week, he has been removed from Cleveland's injury report and will play in Week 10. The Texans' defense is tough on tight ends, having allowed the fourth-fewest fantasy PPG to the position. Still, consider Fannin to be a TE1 this week in a game where the Browns might be trailing and needing to throw.

Denzel Boston, WR, Browns (toe): Boston missed practice on Thursday before returning Friday. He is questionable for Week 10, but HC Todd Monken said on Friday that Boston is "trending in the right direction." On paper, Boston has a favorable matchup against the Texans, although they have been tougher as of late. He is in the WR3/flex range. If he were to sit, KC Concepcion gets the biggest boost and would be in a similar range as Boston. Fannin, albeit in a tough matchup, would also likely see a few more targets.

David Montgomery, RB, Texans (groin): Montgomery returned to practice in a limited fashion Thursday before upgrading to full on Friday. He is listed as questionable, but his participation gives him a chance to suit up in Week 10. Woody Marks popped up on the injury report with a knee injury suffered at practice on Wednesday. He missed Thursday but is not on the final injury report, meaning he will play this Sunday. If Montgomery plays, he's the top option. Either way, the Texans' starting RB is no more than a flex option in a favorable matchup against the Browns, who have allowed the third-most rushing yards per game to the position.

Bhayshul Tuten, RB, Jaguars (ankle/foot):  Despite missing practice this week, Tuten is off the practice report and will play in Week 10. Tuten should be started in fantasy this week. The lone concern is the potential for him to see a reduced workload (just like last week). That would especially be the case if the Jaguars pull ahead, which is very likely against the Titans.

Jakobi Meyers, WR, Jaguars (ankle):  Meyers returned to practice Thursday and is off the injury report, meaning he will play in Week 10. Meyers has played through a number of injuries this season. He is a flex option for those in deeper leagues. The Titans have allowed the most WR fantasy PPG and allow explosive pass plays at the third-highest rate.

Kenneth Walker III, RB, Chiefs (groin): Walker sat out Friday's practice, which always adds concern. Andy Reid said the Chiefs will "see how he feels" before making a call for Sunday. If he suits up, even with limited touches, he should be started in fantasy football. That would also make Emmett Johnson a flex option, as he would likely see a bump in usage. Johnson becomes a "must start" if Walker is ruled out.

Garrett Wilson, WR, Jets (concussion): After sitting out Week 9, Wilson has been limited at practice and is questionable for Week 10. If Wilson suits up, fantasy managers should start him as a WR2. While he has been up and down, the Bills are allowing the 10th-most WR fantasy PPG. Plus, the Jets are likely to be playing from behind in this one and, thus, will have to throw.

Omar Cooper Jr., WR, Jets (ankle): Cooper was limited at practice this week before upgrading to full on Friday. He is questionable for Week 10. If Cooper plays, he'd be in the WR3 range but with much more upside. Cooper saw 11 targets last week and has surpassed 13 fantasy points in three of his past four games, including two 22-point efforts. Plus, Geno Smith should be very effective airing the ball out against a Bills secondary that has been very leaky at times. Adonai Mitchell (knee) popped onto the injury report Friday and is also questionable for the Jets.

Travis Etienne Jr, WR, Saints (hamstring): Etienne, who has not played since Week 3, was limited at practice this week before upgrading to full participation Friday. Nevertheless, he is questionable for Week 10. If he suits up, do not be surprised if he has a reduced workload in his first game back. Even so, he would be in the RB2 range against the Panthers, who rank top-two in terms of the most rushing TDs and fantasy RB PPG allowed. If he sits, Audric Estime would be a streaming option worth starting in 12-team leagues.

-->

Players with late starts
Bam Knight, RB, Cardinals (concussion): Knight has cleared the league's concussion protocol and will play in Week 10. Expect him to handle the bulk of early-down opportunities. Tyler Allgeier is the preferred fantasy play because he handles passing downs on a team that will likely throw often. Still, both are just flex options. Trey McBride is the only Cardinal who should be started this week.

George Pickens, WR, Cowboys (hamstring): Pickens has been limited at practice but was removed from the injury report, meaning he will play Sunday. Even though he has not duplicated his success from last season, Pickens is still good enough that when he plays, you start him in fantasy. If he were to sit, Ryan Flournoy becomes a streaming option in what could be a high-scoring game against the 49ers.

Deebo Samuel Sr., WR, 49ers (hamstring): Samuel has practiced in a limited fashion this week and has been removed from the injury report, meaning he will play in Week 10. He is a WR3/flex play with upside against the Cowboys, who have allowed the seventh-most WR fantasy PPG. The 49ers will be without Mike Evans this week but did add Keenan Allen at the trade deadline. Expect Allen to be used only in a limited fashion for his first game with a new team.

Drew Lock, QB, Seahawks (right elbow/oblique): Lock had been limited at practice this week but has since been removed from the injury report, meaning he will play in Week 10. He's a streaming option for those in need of a bye week/injury replacement. He faces the Raiders, who have allowed the most passing touchdowns and third-most QB fantasy PPG.

Players on Sunday night
No fantasy relevant injuries of note.

Players on Monday night
Ladd McConkey, WR, Chargers (back spasms): Twice in the past five weeks, McConkey has been active for his game but did not play a single snap. Last week, fantasy managers did not know he would not be playing until after kickoff. Simply put, it's very tough to trust him -- especially since McConkey did not practice to start the week and this game is on Monday night. Sitting all your Chargers is probably the way to go.

Ruled out before Sunday
Michael Wilson, WR, Cardinals (neck): Wilson has been placed on IR and is out for the rest of the season. Arizona's receivers moving forward are Reggie Virgil, Simi Fehoko, Devin Duvernay with Zay Jones, Phillip Dorsett II and James Proche II on the practice squad. The preferred options would be Virgil and Jones (if he's elevated). However, this is a situation to avoid unless you are both in a deep league and desperate.

Gardner Minshew II, QB, Cardinals (elbow): Minshew has also been placed on the IR and is out for the rest of the season. It will be Carson Beck starting moving forward for Arizona. He's worth an add in 2-QB formats, but even there, he is just "depth" until we see otherwise. For the time being, consider the Cardinals' offensive motto to be "McBride or bust" and act accordingly.

Jake Ferguson, TE, Cowboys (knee/ankle): Ferguson is out for Week 10 and might miss multiple weeks. That likely means more volume for the Cowboys trio of WRs and makes Ryan Flournoy a more appealing flex option. Go with the replacement options listed above if you need a TE this week.

Marvin Harrison Jr, WR, Texans (hamstring): Harrison was limited Wednesday before missing practice Thursday, which indicates that he was likely injured during practice. He has since been ruled out for Week 10. That makes Tank Dell a bit more appealing. However, he would still be no more than a "boom or bust" option.

Puka Nacua, WR, Rams (knee): Nacua was placed on IR and will miss a minimum of four games. The Rams also placed Jordan Whittington on IR this week (back). That leaves the Rams with Konata Mumpfield and Tutu Atwell as their top receivers. Both are deeper-league flex options. However, I expect a lot of targets to go to the team's RBs and TEs. Both Kyren Williams and Blake Corum should be started this week, while Higbee is a streaming option.

Malik Willis, QB, Dolphins (groin): Willis was placed on the IR this week, meaning he will miss a minimum of four games. The Dolphins will start Kyle McCord in his place. For the time being, fantasy managers should avoid all Dolphins pass catchers. Ollie Gordon II is the lone Miami player worth starting this week. The Colts D/ST is a solid streaming option against the McCord-led Dolphins.

T.J. Hockenson, TE, Vikings (chest/wrist): Hockenson has not practiced this week and is out for Week 10. This likely means even more volume for Justin Jefferson and Jordan Addison, who is listed as questionable with a thumb injury. Some potential alternatives for Hockenson are Hunter Henry, Darren Waller and Tyler Higbee.

Carnell Tate, WR, Titans (shoulder): Coming out of the bye week, Tate has still not practiced. He has been ruled out for Week 10. Expect Wan'Dale Robinson to get a boost in targets. The Titans are likely going to be trailing and will need to throw plenty in a game facing a Jaguars team that has allowed the most WR receiving yards per game. That's enough to make Robinson a flex option in 12-team leagues.

NBA Cup FAQ: Everything to know
What is the format?

NBA commissioner Adam Silver has had a longstanding fascination with European soccer. Establishing an in-season cup competition within the NBA schedule came from soccer leagues having both a regular-season title, won by the team with the most points over the full year, and a separate tournament (or, in some leagues, multiple tournaments) that runs concurrently with the league season.

In England, for example, there are the various divisions -- led by the Premier League -- and also the FA Cup competition. But unlike those European leagues, which play their cup competitions outside of their league schedules, the NBA Cup is built in to the regular-season slate.

The 30 NBA teams are split into six five-team groups -- three featuring Eastern Conference teams and three comprising Western Conference teams -- with each team then playing one game against the other four in its group. The winner of each group, plus the team with the best record among the non-group winners, advances to the knockout stage of the competition.

How will this impact the regular-season schedule and standings?

Typically, the NBA sends out a full 82-game schedule in mid-August. Now, the league sends out only 80 games and leaves a gap of roughly a week to fill in later, depending on how the group stage of the NBA Cup plays out.

The two teams from the East and West that lose in the quarterfinals will play their 82nd game against each other. Meanwhile, the 22 teams that fail to qualify for the knockout rounds will have their final two games scheduled -- one at home and one on the road against others eliminated in the group stage.

The teams that reach the NBA Cup final will actually play 83 games -- though the championship game won't count toward the standings or any statistical markers. The four teams that reach the semifinals will have completed their 82 games and won't need any other games added to their schedule.

Any team that makes it to the semifinals will have that game moved later in the schedule to avoid back-to-back games. The NBA made this change in an effort to avoid having empty days on the calendar while attempting to minimize back-to-backs for all teams as much as possible.

Where are the semifinals and final being played?

In a shift from previous tournaments, the quarterfinals and semifinals will be played at home sites. The Dec. 11 title game, meanwhile, will move from Las Vegas to the storied Hinkle Fieldhouse in Indianapolis. NBA commissioner Adam Silver previously said the league was searching for "storied college arenas" to play host to the Cup final. (No venue has been announced for 2027.)

Why does the NBA Cup include regular-season games?

Before its launch, one of the main questions surrounding the in-season tournament was why any team would be incentivized to compete in it. The NBA ensured teams will be motivated by making every game part of the season and, as in-conference matchups, potentially important to playoff tiebreakers. If this had been set up like the cup tournaments in European soccer, there would have been nothing stopping NBA teams from opting out by sitting their top players for extra rest.

Which teams make up the groups?

To create the groups, the NBA put the 15 teams in each conference into five pots, separated by their finish last season. Pot 1 included the teams that finished in the top three in the regular-season standings, Nos. 4-6 in the standings went into Pot 2, Nos. 7-9 into Pot 3, Nos. 10-12 into Pot 4 and Nos. 13-15 into Pot 5. Does one group stand out the most from the others?

East Group B is a monster.

All five teams -- defending NBA Cup and Finals champion New York, Philadelphia, Cleveland, Miami and Indiana -- are among the favorites to win the conference in 2026-27. The group stage will also feature reunion games for LeBron James, when the 76ers face the Cavs and Heat. And after guard Tyrese Haliburton missed the entire 2025-26 season while rehabbing a torn Achilles, the Pacers will be back among the East elite and hungry to reach the title game in Indianapolis.

What do players get for winning?

In 2023, the first year the tournament was held, the players on the winning team received $500,000 each and the runners-up got $200,000. The losing players of the semifinals each got $100,000, and those ousted in the quarterfinals got $50,000. Now, in each subsequent year, the prizes will be slightly higher, as a result of negotiated raises year over year to keep pace with increases in the salary cap and basketball-related income as part of the most recent collective bargaining agreement between the NBA and the National Basketball Players Association.

Will anyone earn individual honors for their play in NBA Cup games?

There will be an MVP award, as well as an all-tournament team.

Will this have any impact on the playoffs?

Not beyond the games counting in the regular-season standings (and toward tiebreakers). The only playoff impact comes from the wins and losses accrued throughout the tournament. Though there was debate among league insiders about guaranteeing a playoff berth for winning the tournament, ultimately that idea (or any other to further incentivize teams) was not enacted.

Why is it called the Emirates NBA Cup?

The league struck a sponsorship deal with Emirates, the Dubai-based airline, to sponsor the tournament after its initial run. The NBA said last year that it went with the most basic titles for both the tournament and its trophy -- the "in-season tournament" and "NBA Cup" -- as a way to introduce the concept to fans. However, using such nondescript names had another clear advantage: It gave the league a blank slate in case it sold the naming rights for the tournament and cup to a sponsor and avoided the complications that could arise by naming them after someone (for example, late NBA commissioner David Stern, one possibility that had been floated before the tournament was officially unveiled).

stories.headline: Sources: San Jose Earthquakes sold for $625 million to Heath Freeman
stories.summary: Alden Global Capital co-founder Heath Freeman is purchasing the San Jose Earthquakes from John Fisher, following MLS owners' approval of the sale Thursday.
stories.body:
The San Jose Earthquakes announced that Alden Global Capital co-founder Heath Freeman will acquire the team, as well as the club's home venue, PayPal Park, from John Fisher.

Sources confirmed a report from Sportico that the sale reflects an enterprise value of $625 million. The MLS board of governors unanimously approved the transfer of ownership Thursday, noting that the transaction will close in the coming weeks.

The deal will complete a lengthy sales process that began in June 2025. Investment bank Moelis helped facilitate the deal.

"My family and I are honored and humbled to be the next generation owners of the San Jose Earthquakes. I would like to thank John Fisher and the Fisher family for their confidence in me. I know how much they love this team and we expect to continue making them proud in this new era of the Quakes," Freeman said.

"Our vision is simple - winning on and off the field for San Jose and the entire region. The Bay Area is home to some of the world's great institutions, sports franchises and leaders. The standard has been set. We are eager to partner with and connect our community more closely with the Earthquakes and immerse them in our world."

The Quakes struggled during much of Fisher's tenure as owner, reaching the postseason just four times in the past 11 seasons. This season, under manager Bruce Arena, San Jose is in the MLS Cup Playoffs. It will face Houston Dynamo FC in Round 1 when it hosts Game 1 of the best-of-three series Nov. 24 at PayPal Park. The club won the 2012 Supporters' Shield.

"We are committed to investing in the team and building a club that consistently competes for championships," Freeman said. "Off the field, we are equally focused on strengthening our connections with fans and communities in San Jose and throughout the Bay Area. We believe the future of the Earthquakes is incredibly bright, and we can't wait to get started and take the Quakes to unforeseen heights."

Freeman has served as president of Alden Global Capital since 2014. He currently serves as chairman of Tribune Enterprises LLC, which owns and manages newspapers including the Chicago Tribune and South Florida Sun Sentinel, and as vice chairman of MNG Enterprises Inc., which manages newspapers such as The Denver Post, the Mercury News and the Boston Herald. Alden Global Capital has recently enacted deep cost cuts across its publications, leading to multiple layoffs.

Fisher has owned the Earthquakes since 2007, when he and Lew Wolff purchased an expansion team to replace the side that relocated to Houston after the 2005 season. During his tenure, he privately financed the construction of PayPal Park.

"My family and I have loved owning this club for almost 20 years and we are extremely grateful for the support of our amazing fans as well as the hard work of all of our coaches, players and staff," Fisher said. "We would like to thank Jared Shawlee and the executive staff for their leadership and the entire Quakes front office for their commitment to the club, the fans and the community."

"I want to thank John Fisher and his family for their nearly two decades of commitment to the San Jose Earthquakes, Major League Soccer and the Bay Area soccer community," said MLS commissioner Don Garber.

"John has been a great partner and a good friend, and his leadership and investment helped build a strong foundation for the club. Heath Freeman is an ambitious owner with a strong belief in the Earthquakes and the Bay Area as one of the country's great soccer markets. We are excited to welcome him to MLS and look forward to the energy and vision he will bring to this next chapter of the club."

Two MLS teams remain on the market. The Saputo family announced plans to sell CF Montréal earlier this week. The Vancouver Whitecaps are also still on the market, with Goldman Sachs leading that process.

BMO Capital Markets is managing the CF Montréal sale as lead financial adviser, with National Bank of Canada Capital Markets as co-adviser.

stories.headline: Blue Jays' Anthony Santander apologizes for sharing anti-Muslim posts
stories.summary: Blue Jays outfielder Anthony Santander apologized for sharing anti-Muslim social media posts, saying it caused hurt and fell short of his own convictions.
stories.body:
Toronto Blue Jays outfielder Anthony Santander apologized Friday for sharing anti-Muslim social media posts, saying the content caused hurt and fell short of his own convictions.

In a statement on Instagram, Santander said reflection and conversations with people he trusts made him recognize that he should have been more thoughtful about what he shared and the responsibility that comes with having a public voice.

"I realize that this content caused hurt and I sincerely apologize," Santander said in his statement.

He expressed respect for the Muslim community and pledged to avoid sharing content that promotes hate.

"As a man of faith, it is my belief that every person deserves to be treated with dignity and respect, regardless of their religion, background, or beliefs," Santander said. "After hearing feedback from those I hurt, I realize that the content I shared fell short of my own convictions."

Santander shared the posts Nov. 4 and deleted them the next morning, including a video of a Christian preacher disparaging Muslims and another suggesting Sharia law would be imposed on the United States after Abdul El-Sayed's election to the Senate in Michigan.

His apology came a day after Blue Jays president and chief executive officer Mark Shapiro apologized to the Muslim community and fans following a meeting with community leaders, and after general manager Ross Atkins asked Santander to publicly address the controversy.

The 32-year-old Venezuelan player signed a $92.5 million, five-year contract with Toronto in January 2025 but missed the entire 2026 season because of injuries. It remains unclear whether the team will discipline him over the posts.

stories.headline: Six from Team Nurmagomedov, eight in all get prison time over Dvalishvili brawl
stories.summary: Six members of Usman Nurmagomedov's team and two people who filmed the hotel fight also involving Merab Dvalishvili have been handed six-month prison sentences in Abu Dhabi.
stories.body:
Six members of Team Nurmagomedov have been sentenced to six months in prison following a brawl involving former UFC champion Merab Dvalishvili in an Abu Dhabi hotel.

On Wednesday at the host hotel of a Real American Fighting event, PFL lightweight champion Usman Nurmagomedov, the cousin of retired MMA legend Khabib Nurmagomedov, approached Dvalishvili from behind and slapped him, triggering a larger altercation between members of the two camps.

Police arrested and detained all parties. Dvalishvili was later released, according to RAF CEO Chad Bronstein.

According to the Abu Dhabi Judicial Department, six members of Nurmagomedov's team were each sentenced to six months in prison, fined 300,000 AED (approximately $81,700) and ordered to be deported after serving their sentences. According to The National news outlet in the United Arab Emirates, Dvalishvili and a friend were fined 50,000 AED (approximately $13,600) for "disturbing public security and assaulting others."

Two individuals who filmed the altercation also received six-month prison sentences, according to The National, for violating privacy laws by filming and publishing footage of the incident. The court confiscated their phones to delete footage.

Dvalishvili addressed the incident in a social media post Friday, confirming he was released and writing that he is "good, healthy and ready to go." He added that he was hoping everyone involved in the altercation would be released.

Tensions have escalated between Dvalishvili and Team Nurmagomedov since Dvalishvili defeated Umar Nurmagomedov, Usman's older brother, in a UFC bantamweight title fight in January 2025. The two camps had another, smaller altercation at an RAF event in the nation of Georgia in July.

Umar Nurmagomedov was scheduled to wrestle former UFC champion Urijah Faber at the RAF event Saturday but has been replaced by Dvalishvili's 21-year-old Georgian friend Saba Lazishvili, who was involved in the hotel brawl Wednesday. Dvalishvili will still compete in his scheduled bout against former UFC champion Marlon Moraes.

Usman Nurmagomedov, 28, recently fought out his exclusive contract with the PFL, and there had been speculation around the possibility of the undefeated fighter signing with the UFC.

UFC CEO Dana White commented on the brawl Thursday during a news conference in New York.

"What a bunch of f---ing idiots," White said. "It's absolutely ridiculous and stupid, and they're all in jail. That is not a place to go f--- around."

stories.headline: Fantasy hockey rankings: Kochetkov rises to fifth, three Oilers lead overall
stories.summary: Pyotr Kochetkov rises, Connor McDavid is still the fantasy hockey rankings leader after his red-hot start.
stories.body:
On Friday the 13th, the scariest mask in the league belongs to Pyotr Kochetkov. He climbs from No. 36 to No. 5 to become the top goalie in fantasy. Still, nothing is scarier than the Edmonton trio of Connor McDavid, Leon Draisaitl and Evan Bouchard, who hold the top three spots.

stories.headline: Las Vegas Grand Prix 2026: Race start time, how to watch, full schedule, predictions
stories.summary: Formula 1 is back under the bright lights of Las Vegas for one of the most extravagant weekends on the calendar.
stories.body:
Formula 1 is back under the bright lights of Las Vegas for one of the most extravagant weekends on the calendar.

Lando Norris clinched his third victory this season at the São Paulo Grand Prix after new world champion Kimi Antonelli spun out of the lead in wet conditions.

Max Verstappen had a masterful drive in his Red Bull and charged his way through the field from 21st to second.

So you don't miss a thing, here's everything you need to know for the 21st round.

Las Vegas Grand Prix schedule
All times in GMT

Final Practice: 00.30 a.m. - 1.30 a.m.

Qualifying: 4 a.m. - 5 a.m.

Las Vegas Grand Prix: 4 a.m.

How to watch

Every practice and qualifying session as well as the race itself will be available to watch on Sky Sports F1. The sessions are also on Sky Sports Main Event.

For non-subscribers, highlights of the Las Vegas Grand Prix will be on free-to-air television on Channel 4.

In the U.S., subscribers can watch every session on Apple TV, via a new F1 channel on the platform.

Las Vegas Strip Circuit
Las Vegas' race is certainly one of the most newest and flashiest street races with one of the most famous backdrops in the world after it took a spot on the F1 calendar in 2023, costing around $500 million.

The street circuit is one of few night races on the calendar, and includes the city's famous Strip and different landmarks around the city, such as the Bellagio and the Sphere.

The best place to watch the action unfold is from a casino, or West Harmon Zone grandstands. Casinos offer high-end packages to watch in specially built race zones around the circuit, but the grandstands around the final corner and viewing the pit straight still offer a great view.

Las Vegas Grand Prix

Circuit: Las Vegas Strip Circuit; Las Vegas, Nevada

Previous winners in Las Vegas

2024: George Russell (Mercedes)

Other key stats

First F1 race: 2023

Laps: 50 laps of 4km

Lap record: 1:33.365, Max Verstappen (2023)

Most wins: Verstappen has the most wins with two (2023 and 2025) and George Russell has one.

Most poles: Charles Leclerc (2023), Russell (2024) and Norris (2025).

Weather forecast

The weather for the Las Vegas Grand Prix is cold with temperatures between 10-14°C.

What happened last time out?

McLaren's Norris continued his impressive form in the business end of the season and put in a blistering lap to take pole position.

But come Sunday's race he ran wide at the first corner in an attempt to hold off Red Bull's Verstappen, who took advantage from second to gain the lead.

The Dutchman controlled the lead from that point onwards to win the Las Vegas Grand Prix.

Norris and Oscar Piastri ended up being disqualified from the race for a technical infringement -- a major blow in the title race with only two races to go at the time.

Who will win this year?

Mercedes completed the double and wrapped up the constructors' championship last time out, a week after Antonelli was crowned world champion.

With it being a night race, the conditions in Las Vegas are always very cold, a world away from some of the soaring temperatures the drivers race in throughout the year.

McLaren has been running a heavily-upgraded car that seems to be working well, and Norris will be carrying his winning momentum to Vegas.

Verstappen is in strong form and has made his way to second in the title standings with three victories under his belt and 12 podiums this year.

Having won twice in Vegas already, the Dutchman will certainly be the one to watch.

stories.headline: Despite injury and illness, Gus Teixeira is still one of this year's top prospects
stories.summary: Gus Teixeira spent much of his top-age year battling injury and illness, but still found a way to be in contention to be the top pick in the open pool, writes Japser Chellappah.
stories.body:
Gustavo Teixeira had a brilliant top-age campaign. He's worked his way into pick 1 conversations, and is locked into the first handful of selections on draft night.

His success is made all the more impressive considering what's played out behind the scenes.

"I had the ankle injury at the start of the year in the first praccy game," Teixeira tells ESPN.

"It was kind of a bit annoying because every week I thought I'd be playing but it just got pushed back. I had the calf injury, I was out for five or six weeks. I rehabbed that, played a game and then the foot pulled up sore and that's why I'm not testing [at the AFL Draft combine].

"I've also been sick for basically the whole year with a virus."

Teixeira, a powerful forward-half midfielder, played valiantly through glandular fever-like symptoms that didn't get diagnosed until the conclusion of the National Championships.

He was playing games deep in the forward 50 but still finding himself short of breath and unable to hit top gear. After being diagnosed with a severe iron deficiency and receiving an infusion he felt the energy he'd been lacking return, but not before a calf injury linked to his virus took Teixeira out for all but one game in the back half of the season.

Most top-10 chances at the AFL Draft thrive off injury-free seasons where they can continually put their name up in lights. Teixeira couldn't do that this year, so he made his moments count.

His first game back from an ankle concern was in a Vic Metro trial game where he showed his worth, kicking two goals from 20 disposals in a best afield display.

"It was a good day out, I was pretty happy with that. It was annoying I couldn't do a bit more of that throughout the year but I'm sure I can do that in the future."

Teixeira had locked himself into Metro's National Championships outfit by halftime, showing off the power and class that recruiters covet.

At the National Championships he was playing under duress from his undiagnosed virus, but he still took the opportunity to show his value deep in attack.

"Obviously I was sick so I was resting a bit, I was sore the first week and they wanted me to play more forward. I kicked a few goals and they wanted me to stay down forward and that's where I was able to impact the most," he tells ESPN.

Teixeira claimed All-Australian honours, booting seven goals in his four outings including a best on ground demolition of the Allies where he kicked four goals from 22 touches.

It was an element of his game that proved his worth outside of the centre square. Teixeira got to dangerous spots and created separation with proactive running, and from there was able to demonstrate his cleanliness and class to make his chances count.

"I've always thought I want to be a midfielder, I want to play in there. Skills are very important as a midfielder so you've got to be clean and you've got to be able to kick. I'm just chipping away at it and improving."

Teixeira is of Brazilian descent via his father Matt, who was born in the city of Belo Horizonte before moving to Australia when he was 25.

He brings Gus back to Brazil every year, and that connection to a non-English speaking country would allow Teixeira to join zoned club St Kilda's Next Generation Academy if not for friction points within the AFL's own NGA rules.

"Belo Horizonte is just inland of Rio... It's like the size of Melbourne but no one's really heard of it. It's a fully different culture and it's always great to go back," he explains.

"The AFL changed the rules for the regions this year, so they allow South American people this year but you need to be in it for three years. I would've only been in it for a year... my younger siblings are in it now. I've got a brother, Eddie, who's 12 and my sister Lucy who's 14."

Like a host of the top prospects this year, Teixeira has been an Essendon supporter his whole life. The Bombers have the top pick and Teixeira is within that bracket of the pool.

"I haven't thought about the Bombers pick-wise, but just the club and thinking about what it would be like obviously going to the Bombers, it'd be great at the moment. They're getting in some good coaches and they've got some good players coming through.

"Really though I'd be stoked to get drafted to any club, moving interstate would be a pretty cool experience. I'm always trying to get the best out of myself, I've always tried to be the best at everything and just put my best foot forward so I'll do that anywhere."

stories.headline: Dirk Kuyt leaves Fenerbahce a week after defeating Liverpool
stories.summary: Dirk Kuyt left Fenerbahce on Wednesday, one week after guiding the team as interim coach to beat his old club Liverpool in the Champions League.
stories.body:
ISTANBUL -- Dirk Kuyt left Fenerbahce on Wednesday, one week after guiding the team as interim coach to beat his old club Liverpool in the Champions League.

The former Netherlands forward took charge of that 3-2 win in Istanbul despite the club already having made a deal with Emre Belözoğlu to take over.

Kuyt returned in July to Fenerbahce, where he played from 2012-15, to assist coach Ismail Kartal who resigned last month.

"We thank you from the bottom of our hearts for all that you have contributed to these colors," Fenerbahce said in a social media post announcing Kuyt's exit. "Today we say goodbye to you but your place in this big family will never change."

Belözoğlu, a former captain of the club, takes over a team sixth in the Turkish league and 19th in the 36-team Champions League standings.

Fenerbahce's next Champions League opponent is Shakhtar Donetsk in London on Nov. 25.

stories.headline: Why Kiwi sharp-shooter is taking Cup final personally
stories.summary: Jamayne Isaako is on a remarkable personal run entering the World Cup final, where he has a score to settle with an NRL teammate.
stories.body:
Jamayne Isaako is taking it personally as a generational New Zealand team attempts to break Australia's World Cup stranglehold in their Brisbane decider.

The Kiwis will face the Kangaroos at Suncorp Stadium on Sunday, attempting to win a second cup and first since 2008.

The hosts have won nine of the last 10 tournaments but will be challenged by a side that did everything but win in a 24-22 loss to begin the tournament.

Australian winger Jack Bostock scored a hat trick on debut, twice leaping above Dolphins teammate Isaako for tries while also plucking an intercept.

Isaako, who will leave for the Melbourne Storm next season after 11 campaigns with Brisbane's, Gold Coast's and Redcliffe's NRL clubs, hasn't forgotten.

"Not to take him lightly," Isaako said of what he took from that duel.

"It wasn't something I incorporated into my prep; his height and reach there.

"So it's something I'll be taking personally this weekend, hopefully I can stop him and do a better job."

Bostock played in the centres - on the same side of the field as Isaako - in the New Zealander's last season at the Dolphins and the pair were able to laugh about the contest when they reunited for a photo-shoot this week.

"He gave me a little bit of stick," Isaako said.

The 30-year-old maintains belief is high, pointing to the side's 2023 Pacific Champions triumph as a turning point for the team and himself. The goal-kicker was left out of the Kiwis side for four years before his 2023 return and has played 13 consecutive Test and 98 consecutive NRL games since.

"There's a lot of confidence about what we've been able to create here," he said.

"I don't think we're ever going to get a squad (this good) again, so it's about making the most of the moments we get together.

"I'm certainly going to miss this place (living in Brisbane) and I'd like to finish on a high, hopefully holding the World Cup."

stories.headline: Seahawks are hurting with injuries, but two players will return vs. Raiders
stories.summary: QB Drew Lock will start again for Darnold. LB Uchenna Nwosu and WR Rashid Shaheed will return to the field in Las Vegas.
stories.body:
RENTON, Wash. - Seattle Seahawks coach Mike Macdonald said Drew Lock had a good week of practice as he prepares to fill in again for Sam Darnold on Sunday against the 4-5 Las Vegas Raiders (4:05 p.m. ET, CBS) -- this time despite a pair of ailments of his own.

Lock was already dealing with an injury to his right elbow when he hurt his oblique last Sunday in Seattle's 17-3 win over the Arizona Cardinals. He was again limited in practice all week, as has been the case since the start of Week 6.

"Similar cadence in workload in terms of last week," Macdonald said Friday. "It's good to have done it and gotten through the week well. I know he's confident and optimistic, so we're in good shape."

In addition to Darnold (quad, rib) and left guard Quenton Nelson (knee) -- whom Macdonald had ruled out earlier in the week -- the Seahawks will be without defensive tackle Leonard Williams (stinger) and left tackle Charles Cross (ankle) again Sunday.

They'll get outside linebacker Uchenna Nwosu (ankle) and wide receiver/kick returner Rashid Shaheed (knee) back against the Raiders after each missed the past two games. Defensive tackle Jarran Reed will play Sunday after missing two days this week to tend to a personal matter.

Lock said Thursday that he was feeling good, and that his oblique injury wasn't impacting his throwing all that much. It's on his right side, which Lock said is "way better" for a right-handed quatrerback than a left oblique injury, which caused him to miss two weeks during the preseason when he was with the New York Giants in 2024.

"I feel like we did a great job handling the week last week, and here we are, we've just got a little something added to it, and I think we're doing the same," Lock said. "We're doing a great job getting ready."

Macdonald volunteered that No. 3 quarterback Jalen Milroe "has done a tremendous job" while taking reps with the Seahawks' No. 1 offense as the team continues to manage Lock's workload in practice.

Sunday's game will mark Lock's third start this season and the fourth time he's stepped in for Darnold, who hurt his glute on the fifth play of the opener, then suffered a cracked rib and a quad injury in Week 8.

Macdonald has said Darnold might be able to return for the Seahawks' game against the San Francisco 49ers in Week 12, following their bye.

"I see Sam progressing with his rehab," Macdonald said. "The guys are saying he's doing a great job and he's progressing. We'll take it a day and a week at a time."

Williams will miss his second straight game due to a stinger. He took part in pre-practice warmups on Wednesday and Thursday but was listed as a non-participant all week.

"It's more of a contact thing," Macdonald said. "So he's done a good job of staying in shape and staying fresh. He's in the meetings. He's doing all the Leo things. He's just not playing right now."

Josh Jones will make a third consecutive start at left tackle for Cross, who also did not practice this week. Macdonald said Cross should be ready for the 49ers game on Nov. 29.

stories.headline: Lakers' Austin Reaves day-to-day with left heel bruise
stories.summary: Lakers guard Austin Reaves is considered day-to-day as he deals with a left heel bruise, coach JJ Redick said Friday.
stories.body:
EL SEGUNDO, Calif. -- Los Angeles Lakers guard Austin Reaves is considered day-to-day as he deals with a left heel bruise, coach JJ Redick said after practice Friday.

Reaves left L.A.'s 123-112 victory over the Milwaukee Bucks on Wednesday midway through the third quarter and did not return after landing awkwardly on his left foot after missing a contested fast-break dunk.

Reaves underwent X-rays at the arena Wednesday that came back clean. After seeing how Reaves was feeling Thursday morning once the Lakers returned to Los Angeles, the team determined that further medical imaging on the shooting guard's foot would not be necessary.

When Redick was asked if Reaves had suffered only a "minor" injury, considering the Lakers decided to forgo an MRI, the coach replied: "I would assume a day-to-day injury is minor, yeah."

Redick provided injury updates on three other Lakers players as well.

Luka Doncic, who turned his right ankle late in the win over the Bucks, "is fine," according to Redick.

"I think the expectation would be he's available," Redick said, referring to L.A.'s next game against the Phoenix Suns on Sunday.

Redick said backup guard Collin Sexton, who required stitches above his right eye after he and Bucks guard Ryan Rollins unintentionally head-butted one another Wednesday, was cleared of any concussion symptoms but is also considered day-to-day.

Guard Quentin Grimes, who sprained the right pinkie on his shooting hand and missed the Lakers' past two games, participated in the live portion of practice Friday, Redick said.

Grimes said he jammed the finger in the Pistons game and taped it up for practice.

"The swelling has gone down a lot," Grimes said. "It's kind of feeling basically back to normal."

The Lakers, at 11-2, own the No. 1 record in the NBA. Redick used the three-day break in the schedule to "audit" the team. He said he had his analytics department prepare a 21-page presentation he used, along with a film session, to discuss L.A.'s defensive and offensive identities before practice Friday.

"It was good," forward Ziaire Williams said of the meeting. "A lot of good things and a lot of things to clean up. Being first in the West, with the stuff that they showed us, you would think we were almost last, you know? But yeah, for sure, got to keep us honest."

stories.headline: Messi to play in Argentina Jan. 19 for Inter Miami-River friendly
stories.summary: Lionel Messi will return to play at Estadio Monumental on Jan. 19 when Inter Miami travel to Buenos Aires to play River Plate.
stories.body:
Lionel Messi will return to play at Estadio Monumental on Jan. 19 for the first time since his Argentina farewell when Inter Miami travels to Buenos Aires to play River Plate in a friendly.

The eight-time Ballon d'Or winner has played a total of 29 matches for Argentina at El Monumental, the most recent on Oct. 6 in his national team farewell, where he played his 208th and final game for Argentina.

That match ended with his 126th goal capping a 21-year career for the legendary No. 10, which included two Copa América titles and a World Cup.

This game will mark the first time Messi has played a club match in his home country.

Over his career he has face Argentina clubs four times, including beating Estudiantes with Barcelona at the 2009 Club World Cup in United Arab Emirates and again when Barcelona defeated River for the 2015 Club World Cup in Japan.

Messi has also played two other friendlies vs. Argentina clubs: In 2018 with Barcelona beating Boca Juniors for the Joan Gamper trophy and a friendly in 2024 vs. his boyhood club, Newell's in Miami, which ended in a 1-1 draw.

River Plate is one of South America's most successful clubs, boasting 38 domestic titles and four Copa Libertadores trophies.

Earlier this week, Messi was named a finalist for the 2026 Major League Soccer MVP award. The Inter Miami captain seeks to become the first player to win the prize on three consecutive occasions.

Messi already clinched a record second straight Golden Boot award after scoring 26 goals in the 2026 regular season.

Miami said they expect Messi to be joined by Casemiro, Rodrigo De Paul, Luis Suárez, Nicolás Otamendi and Thiago Almada for the trip.

Inter Miami's previous preseason tours have included visits to Peru, Ecuador, Colombia and Puerto Rico.

Inter Miami will kick off the 2027 Major League Soccer season on Feb. 19 against FC Cincinnati at Nu Stadium.

stories.headline: 2026-27 MLB free agency, trade grades: Offseason analysis
stories.summary: We've got you covered with grades and analysis on every winter signing and big offseason trade.
stories.body:
Hot stove season has finally begun!

The 2026-27 MLB offseason is officially here, and we have you covered with grades and analysis for every major signing and trade as this winter -- which is expected to include a labor stoppage -- unfolds.

Whether it's a franchise-changing free agent signing or an unexpected blockbuster trade, we'll weigh in with what it all means for next season and beyond.

ESPN MLB experts Bradford Doolittle and David Schoenfield will evaluate each move as it happens, so follow along here -- this story will continue to be updated. Check back in for all the most recent analysis.

Related links: Tracker | Top 50 free agents

Red Sox get offensive boost with Bauers addition

The deal: Four years, $58 million

Grade: A

The Red Sox weren't high on anybody's list of teams likely to sign Jake Bauers given they already have an All-Star first baseman in Willson Contreras, but this signing is an early candidate for best move of the offseason. The grade reflects two thoughts: (1) that Bauers' breakout -- he finished 11th in the majors in OPS and third in on-base percentage this past season -- is for real; and (2) that the contract is a steal at $14.5 million per year.

Bauers will be entering his age-31 season, and, of course, spent years struggling in the majors before finally figuring things out, so while there would generally be concern that his 2026 season was a fluke, all the advanced metrics suggest the opposite. His Statcast numbers: 93rd percentile bat speed, 94th percentile hard-hit rate, 93rd percentile chase rate, 98th percentile walk rate. Those are real skills that aren't going to diminish overnight and should allow him to remain a productive hitter (he even hit left-handers well, so should project as a full-time player). Everyone saw the quality of his at-bats during the postseason throughout the Milwaukee Brewers' title run; he was named MVP of the National League Championship Series.

As for the contract, compare it to Josh Naylor's deal last year, when he signed a five-year, $92.5 million contract with the Seattle Mariners. Naylor was two years younger, but he was coming off a 129-OPS+, 3.0-WAR season compared with Bauers' 140 OPS+ and 3.3 WAR. Yes, Naylor had the longer track record of success but less power and a lower OBP. Signing Bauers for $58 million looks like a potential bargain.

Contreras is under contract for 2027 with a team option for 2028 and is the better fielder, so Bauers slots in as the DH. That leaves Roman Anthony, Ceddanne Rafaela and Wilyer Abreu in the outfield. Masataka Yoshida is still around for one more year as a backup, and the Red Sox will likely look to trade Jarren Duran, who still has two years of team control but is estimated to make $11.1 million in arbitration. With Duran coming off a bad season at the plate, the Red Sox might non-tender him if they can't trade him.

No doubt there will be criticism that the Red Sox needed a right-handed batter instead, but they actually had a slightly higher OPS against left-handers (.734 to .710). They just needed a good hitter, regardless of which side of the plate he stands on.

Remember that they also acquired the right-handed Curtis Mead from the Washington Nationals only to see him get injured in his first game with them. He'll be back and should slot in at second base. Boston also has shortstop Franklin Arias, one of the top three or four prospects in the minors who demolished Double- and Triple-A this year. Indeed, if Bauers comes close to his 2026 numbers and Anthony hits like everyone thought he was going to in 2026, this could be one of the best lineups in the league:

LF Anthony (L)

RF Abreu (L)

1B Contreras (R)

DH Bauers (L)

CF Rafaela (R)

2B Mead (R)

C Adley Rutschman (S)

SS Arias (R) / Trevor Story (R)

3B Caleb Durbin (R)

As for the Brewers, it's sad to see a postseason hero go, although not necessarily unexpected. They could have afforded this contract, but they have first-base prospects just about ready in Andrew Fischer, who led the minors with 48 home runs, and Blake Burke, who hit 34 home runs and stole 29 bases. They also have Andrew Vaughn on hand as a placeholder if Fischer and Burke aren't ready. Plus, they might need this money to sign William Contreras to a long-term extension. The Brewers will be fine. -- Schoenfield

Braves bolster bullpen by landing Phillips
The deal: Three years, $35 million

Grade: B-

The Atlanta Braves don't go after the biggest free agents -- B.J. Upton's $75 million deal in 2013 remains the largest free agent contract in franchise history -- but president of baseball operations Alex Anthopoulos does like to strike as early as possible in the offseason, and he did that again with Evan Phillips.

Phillips will essentially take the roster spot of Raisel Iglesias, so the Braves will get a little younger and maybe a little better, although Iglesias had a good season as the closer in 2026 following some bumps in 2025. The Braves had one of the best bullpens in the majors this past year, leading in win probability added while ranking fourth in ERA and sixth in OPS allowed. Iglesias departs as a free agent, but Didier Fuentes or Robert Suarez can replace him as the ninth-inning guy, with Phillips likely slotting in as a setup man alongside lefties Dylan Lee and Dylan Dodd.

Phillips was one of the best relievers in the majors with the Dodgers in 2022-23 before suffering shoulder and elbow injuries at the end of the 2024 season and finally undergoing Tommy John surgery in June 2025. He returned to make 31 appearances with the Dodgers in 2026, finishing with 33 strikeouts and just six walks in 26 innings. The stuff looked good -- he was throwing a little harder than pre-injury -- although he did serve up five home runs, and his injury history makes a three-year deal a little risky.

The belief was that the Braves' pitching priority this offseason would be a starter, but signing Phillips will allow them to stretch out Fuentes as a starter in spring training. He does have a three-pitch arsenal in his fastball, slider and splitter, and he has thrown a curveball in the past, so as effective as Fuentes was in relief as a rookie in 2026, it makes sense to see if it can work out for him in the rotation. -- Schoenfield

Tigers kick off free agency with Pagan deal

The deal: One year, $11.5 million

Grade: C

A key reason the Detroit Tigers finished 76-86 despite a plus-71 run differential was the bullpen: Despite finishing 12th in ERA, it ranked 26th in win probability added, so it performed worse in high-leverage situations. Out with Kenley Jansen, in with Emilio Pagan, who has been the Reds' closer the past two seasons.

Jansen was only 22-for-28 in saves in 2026, so maybe Pagan is only a small upgrade, but like Jansen, Pagan has been prone to the home run, serving up 17 in 111⅓ innings over the past two seasons. The Tigers are betting that getting out of Cincinnati -- where he allowed 12 of those 17 home runs -- will help. Pagan is a three-pitch reliever, with a splitter that he throws primarily to left-handers and a cutter he throws to right-handers. But his 95 mph fastball is rather pedestrian for a modern closer, and batters have hit 12 home runs off it the past two seasons.

Pagan is also turning 36 years old and his fastball velo dropped from 95.8 mph in 2025 to 94.9 in 2026, so there are a couple of red flags here. The Tigers had to add somebody to the bullpen, and doing so before the anticipated lockout is logical, but Pagan projects as a midtier closer rather than the elite guy Detroit needs. Kyle Finnegan and Will Vest both struggled in 2026, so the Tigers could still nab a reliable right-handed setup guy. -- Schoenfield

stories.headline: UFC 334 preview, picks for Ciryl Gane-Josh Hokit and Kayla Harrison-Amanda Nunes
stories.summary: A look at the matchups and experts' picks for both title fights at UFC 334 in New York City.
stories.body:
One year ago, Josh Hokit was virtually unknown in the fight world. On Saturday, he will headline a UFC event at the iconic Madison Square Garden in New York. One of the biggest questions surrounding him is how much of his soul he's sacrificed to get here. This weekend could provide an answer to an even bigger question.

Hokit (10-0) will challenge heavyweight champion Ciryl Gane (14-2) at UFC 334 (Paramount+, 9 p.m. ET). Hokit, 28, has been one of the sport's biggest breakouts in 2026, thanks in no small part to the controversy he's stirred on the mic. He stood on the South Lawn of the White House in June and made vulgar remarks about former first lady Michelle Obama. He made distasteful 9/11 jokes on social media the same day of the 25th anniversary of the attacks on the very city where he will compete this weekend.

A former collegiate football player at Fresno State University, Hokit has broken character on numerous occasions and said he doesn't even enjoy the attention. But he's using hate and controversy to stand out, and he won't apologize for it. He acknowledged as much again this week, during media appearances in New York.

"I'll never look back and regret it," Hokit said. "I'm here to be remembered. If I have to crack a few eggs to make an omelette, f--- it. If I have to burn the bridge to light the way, f--- it."

Some of Hokit's appalling comments have prompted UFC CEO Dana White to say during an episode of "The Jim Rome Show" on Nov. 4 that he's given Hokit difficult matchups on his way up and that he doesn't like "anything Josh Hokit says." Hokit has taken advantage of the high-profile opportunities he has received this year from White, who's said Hokit earned his title shot on Saturday.

Whether Hokit would tone down his act if he captures a UFC championship -- or double down on it -- remains to be seen. Either way, it does create an intriguing industry-wide storyline to watch on Saturday.

Those who have been offended by Hokit's tactics likely want to see him lose. Such is the effect of him playing a villain.

But there's another reason critics should fear a Hokit victory: It could inspire other fighters to follow his blueprint for success. That could happen, actually, regardless of Saturday's outcome.

More storylines to watch

After 8 years, Kayla Harrison and Amanda Nunes finally settle their differences

From the moment Harrison walked into the American Top Team gym in South Florida in 2018 to begin her MMA career, she and Nunes were on a path to one of the greatest rivalries in women's MMA -- even if it took years for them to call it one.

The history behind the matchup is as compelling as their individual achievements. Harrison says she wanted to build something in the gym alongside Nunes, while Nunes -- already UFC champion when Harrison arrived -- says she recognized from the start that Harrison wanted to take her place in the sport. Those conflicting perceptions created the tension that led to Saturday's bout, with Nunes coming out of a 3½-year retirement to challenge for Harrison's bantamweight belt.

The fight was originally scheduled for January 2026, but Harrison was forced to withdraw just weeks before the bout to undergo two-level spinal fusion surgery for a neck injury she had been dealing with for years.

Stephen 'Wonderboy' Thompson retirement

Thompson was never the only "nice guy" in MMA, but he might have perfected it more than anyone else.

Thompson has announced that Saturday's bout against Charles Radtke will be the end of his 14-year UFC career. It's fitting that his last act will take place in Madison Square Garden, the same building in which his career could have taken a very different path. Thompson fought Tyron Woodley to a majority draw in November 2016 at UFC 205, the promotion's first event in New York City. He came within one round on one judge's scorecard of becoming UFC champion. Thompson lost an immediate rematch to Woodley in 2017, and never returned to title contention after a 2019 loss to Anthony Pettis.

Nevertheless, Thompson left his mark in the sport. He's regarded as one of the most honorable fighters of the past decade. A karate-based welterweight, Thompson continued teaching children's martial arts classes even as an active, ranked fighter in the UFC. His iconic walkouts to Tenacious D's "Wonderboy" and notable wins over Johny Hendricks, Rory MacDonald, Jorge Masvidal and Robert Whittaker will not soon be forgotten.

"I want to leave this sport knowing that, hey, you can still be at the top of the game and be the good guy," Thompson said. "That's a breath of fresh air. You don't have to be the guy to talk trash all the time."

Coaches' questions and predictions for the title fights

Editor's note: Responses have been edited for brevity and clarity.

Ciryl Gane (c) vs. Josh Hokit

How will Hokit handle Gane's size?

I was in Francis Ngannou's corner against Gane, and the first thing I said was, "This is a big f---ing guy who can move." Hokit is smaller, and could probably be a light heavyweight. He needs to wrestle in this fight, and what will grappling a big guy like that do to his gas tank? Gane's stance switches on the feet are big, because they change the wrestling picture. He's always changing his lead leg, which could force Josh to constantly recalculate where his attacks are. Gane will need to mix in anti-wrestling strikes, meaning target some strikes to the chest and body to negate Josh's level changes. Hokit has to cut off the cage and, once he does get Gane down, prioritize controlling his legs to slow the process of him getting back up. I think the size is a real factor, so I'm picking Gane. -- Eric Nicksick, Xtreme Couture

Can Hokit's chaos disrupt the technical superiority of Gane?

This is Hokit's biggest step up, a true test of the elite -- whereas, I do not believe this is the best guy Gane has fought. The question is whether Hokit's off-the-wall pressure, all the s--- he does in there to make it chaotic, can hold up against a technical fighter like Gane. You have to let Hokit do the things that have gotten him to this point. You don't want him to be sloppy, but I wouldn't try to tighten things up too much. I feel like Gane is going to be too much, though, and expose what Hokit is missing technically. Hokit has to make the fight ugly. I feel Gane is too crisp, too clean, and ends up sparking him. Gane by TKO. -- John Wood, Syndicate MMA

Kayla Harrison (c) vs. Amanda Nunes
What do the fighters know that we don't, and how will they use it?

Who got the better of whom in the gym? What do they know intimately about each other that we don't, and how will they use that information? For Amanda, she needs to intercept Kayla's pressure with straight punches. Looping punches allow Kayla to sit down and get into the hips, so those punches scare me. Amanda has to defend the second and third takedown attempts and, if and when she does get taken down, she has to make Kayla work. The issue there is that Amanda has been notorious for her own failed cardio, but she has to make Kayla work for any grappling success. And for Kayla, she can't fight a la carte, which she has done in the past. She can't say, "Now I'm striking; OK, now I'm wrestling." She has to throw strikes to close distance and then blend her wrestling. Prioritize positions over going for submissions and make this a physical fight. I'm going to pick Amanda. I think she wins a decision. -- Eric Nicksick, Xtreme Couture

How will Nunes look after 3½ years away from the Octagon?

Is Nunes still Nunes? Usually in MMA, time off doesn't result in a better, sharper fighter. But Amanda was so dominant and such a beast. I know Amanda personally and I know she wouldn't be coming back if she didn't know she's still got it. I think she will have a good night at the office. It's the power. She has that rare power that can change the outcome of a fight if she hits you just one time. And she's dealt with the pressure that Kayla is going to bring. I know Julianna Peña got Amanda off her game when she beat her in 2021, but I think Amanda went into that fight injured and not caring as much. As long as that's not the case and she comes in ready, just needs to make contact once. Nunes by TKO. -- John Wood, Syndicate MMA

stories.headline: Finland's block on Russian athletes could affect NHL's return
stories.summary: The NHL will consider Finland's plans to prevent Russian athletes from entering the country when deciding whether to stage more regular-season games there in the future, the league told The Associated Press.
stories.body:
The NHL will consider Finland's plans to prevent Russian athletes from entering the country when deciding whether to stage more regular-season games there in the future, the league told The Associated Press.

Finland and Norway both announced plans to refuse entry to Russian athletes Thursday, the same day as the Carolina Hurricanes defeated the Seattle Kraken 4-1 in the first of two NHL regular-season games in the Finnish capital, Helsinki.

The Finnish restrictions take effect Monday, after the NHL games, and follow a backlash to Russia being reinstated in the hockey world championships, which is not an NHL event.

"We are aware of the government's position, and we'll have to take that into account," the league said Friday when asked if the new restrictions would be an obstacle to future games in Finland.

The Finnish foreign ministry's statement outlining the restrictions did not distinguish between Russian athletes on national teams, those competing as neutral athletes or those on club teams in sports like hockey or soccer.

The ministry said Thursday that Russians would be allowed to work in Finland only on "tasks that are essential to Finland's national interests." It added that Russia "uses sports as a propaganda tool."

The NHL has played regular-season games in Finland as part of its Global Series in 2022 and 2024. No future games have yet been announced.

As of the opening day of the 2026-27 season in September, there were 53 Russians on NHL rosters, making up 7.3% of the league. That was the fourth-largest contingent of players from any country.

Russian wing Andrei Svechnikov had an assist for the Hurricanes in Thursday's win. Pyotr Kochetkov was Carolina's backup goaltender. The Hurricanes and Kraken play again in Finland on Saturday.

The government decisions Thursday followed a backlash in Finland to Russia being reinstated for the ice hockey world championships, but its effects could mostly be felt in other sports. The International Skating Union warned of a "possible consequential impact" on its figure skating world championships in Finland in March.

Public broadcaster ERR reported Friday that Estonia had written to the International Ski and Snowboard Federation that athletes from Russia and its ally Belarus would not be allowed to enter the country. Estonia hosts the world junior championships in Nordic skiing in January.

stories.headline: Liam Lawson and Arvid Lindblad to continue at Racing Bulls for 2027
stories.summary: Liam Lawson will stay in Formula 1 alongside teammate Arvid Lindblad at Racing Bulls in 2027, ending weeks of speculation about the New Zealander's future.
stories.body:
Liam Lawson will stay in Formula 1 alongside teammate Arvid Lindblad at Racing Bulls in 2027, ending weeks of speculation about the New Zealander's future.

Lawson's place at the team had been under scrutiny in recent weeks, with Red Bull's Bulgarian junior Nikola Tsolov waiting in the wings.

Racing Bulls ended any doubt on Thursday, confirming Lawson and Lindblad will continue together for another year.

Lawson has been one of the year's standout performers, sitting ninth with 89 points, a run of form which continued with a strong showing at last weekend's São Paulo Grand Prix, where he started third and finished seventh. Rookie teammate Lindblad is 11th with 38.

Racing Bulls is fighting for fifth in the constructors' championship.

- Qatar, Abu Dhabi races set to go ahead as F1 rules out Imola backup plan for finale

- Lewis Hamilton visits Gaza border, urges Israel to 'let the aid trucks in'

Team boss Alan Permane, who last week signed a deal to stay in his role until 2029, said Lawson and Lindblad is the strongest lineup the team could ask for.

"We're delighted to be continuing with Liam and Arvid for 2027," Permane said. "Both have demonstrated their ability and potential throughout the season, and we've seen the progress they've made, both individually and as a pairing. I have no doubt that this is the best driver line-up for us, bringing a strong combination of experience and ambition.

"Together, we have a solid foundation to build on the progress made this year, continue pushing ourselves forward and take the next step towards achieving our ambitions in 2027."

Red Bull has confirmed Tsolov as reserve driver for Red Bull and Racing Bulls in 2027. The 19-year-old currently competes in Formula 2 for Campos Racing and is second in the title standings with two races remaining.

The team are promising an "extensive" programme of free practice sessions and Testing of Previous Car running as allowed under the F1 rulebook.

Tsolov said: "I'm incredibly happy and grateful to Red Bull for giving me this opportunity. Since joining the Junior Team, I've received amazing support and have developed so much, both as a driver and as a person. My career has progressed incredibly quickly, and I owe a lot to everyone who has believed in me and helped me get to this point.

"My ambition is clear: I want to become an F1 driver. Having the opportunity to spend next year preparing for that next step is incredibly exciting. I'm confident that with the Team's support and experience, I'll have the best possible preparation to make sure I'm fully ready to take the next step onto the F1 grid when the time comes."

The 2026 AFL Draft is fast approaching. Marvel Stadium will once more play host to the first round at 7:00pm AEDT on November 19, with the draft recommencing for the second round onwards on November 20.

Key dates and times

State of play and players to know
Essendon will be on the clock first, holding the top selection a decade on from the last time it took the number one pick to the AFL Draft. The Dons are expected to first bid on Port Adelaide-tied forward Dougie Cochrane, which will trigger a start-of-second-round compensation pick for the Bombers, Tigers and Eagles.

There are familial lines drawn throughout an exciting 2008-born cohort. Cody Walker is the son of high-flying Blue Andrew and will be headed to Princes Park. Cochrane is the son of former North Melbourne and Port Adelaide midfielder Stuart, though he isn't eligible to either team under the 100-game father-son rule. Instead, he's eligible to join the Power as part of their Next Generation Academy as an Indigenous prospect.

Top-10 riser Sam Gayfer is the nephew of 1990 premiership Pie Mick, and Koby LeCras brings goalkicking pedigree via 2018 premiership uncle Mark.

There will be up to five club-tied talents picked in the first round of the AFL Draft. But that won't necessarily result in an extended first night. Over the past five years the first round has averaged out to 25 selections accounting for father-son and academy bids, but clubs are expecting a number closer to the traditional 18 picks in the final intake of the 18-team competition.

Stricter stipulations around matching bids is at play, with clubs only able to use a maximum of two selections when matching for a club-tied prospect, meaning the selections of Port Adelaide, Carlton, Brisbane and GWS will be absorbed as early bids are matched.

We could see a record number of Indigenous talents picked in the first round. The high-water mark was four in 2005 and 2014, and all of Cochrane, Walker, Caylen Murray (Lions Academy), Toby Krasna and Jake Eime could be taken in the first round in 2026.

Thirteen of the top prospects have already been invited to Marvel Stadium on November 19.

Ethan Drever, Arki Butler and Heath Mellody are all still in contention to be the open pool No. 1 pick, with Harry Van Hattum, Gus Teixeira, Mitch Harris and Ethan Matthews (Giants Academy) rounding out the group on top of draft boards alongside Cochrane and Walker.

Murray, Gayfer, Wil Malady and Leo Steed have also received invites in a sign of club interest on night one.

Around 65 picks are expected to be taken across both nights which would surpass the 60 selections last year.

stories.headline: Subtle reason Jillaroo will cause Cup final headaches
stories.summary: Jillaroos fullback Tamika Upton has explained why Jesse Southwell commanded selection for the World Cup final against New Zealand.
stories.body:
The numbers are impressive, but it's what doesn't show up on the stats sheet that Tamika Upton likes most about Jesse Southwell.

The Brisbane five-eighth won a tight selection battle to replace Sydney Roosters premiership winner Jocelyn Kelleher for Sunday's Women's World Cup final.

Kelleher started in three of Australia's four Cup games and was player of the match in the 40-0 win over Samoa on Test debut.

Southwell, who will partner Tarryn Aiken in the halves, filled her boots with 44 points of her own in the record-breaking 124-6 win over Wales.

Kelleher kicks goals too and shared a strong bond with Roosters teammate and halfback Aiken during their NRLW title win, but has been named in the 21 jersey for the clash with New Zealand.

"Tarryn and Jesse haven't played too much footy together, but I've been fortunate to play a lot with the both of them and watching them both link up is going to be pretty special," Australia and Brisbane fullback Upton said.

"The best thing about Jesse, and this goes unnoticed and without stats, is how much space she creates for the people outside of her.

"I've been fortunate enough to have that pretty much my whole career, and I'm excited for her to do that for Taryn and make her job a little bit easier.

"She's young, she's energetic, she's enthusiastic, she wants the ball and she wants to be a part of the game."

Australia cruised into the final four before receiving a welcome test in their comeback semi-final defeat of Fiji.

"The record-breaking games are probably not the best when you're prepping for finals footy, which is so different," Upton said.

"We've had the luxury of everything working out for us and that just doesn't happen when it comes to finals.

"So it was good to be under the pump."
